note.explanation: A system is a group of related parts that work together in an environment to achieve a purpose. Its objective tells us what it is meant to do; its components do the work, and communication helps them cooperate.
examples: A car has parts such as an engine, wheels and brakes. Each part has a task, and together they help the car move.
A computer system processes data to provide useful information to users.
note.checkAnswer: A system has objectives, components, communication among components, and an environment. Its components communicate to achieve its objective.
note.simple: A system is a team of connected parts working together for a purpose.
note.checkQuestion: What are the basic features used to describe a system?
note.title: Understanding Systems
steps: Identify the system's objective: what does it aim to do?

written.text: Define and describe the concept of a system. Explain the fundamental components, objectives, environment, and methods of communication within a system.
written.finalAnswer: A system is an organized set of components coordinated to perform a designated function. It has an objective or goal, components that each play a role, communication among components, and an environment of external factors that interact with it. The components communicate and interact to achieve the system's objective; systems also interact with their environment through inputs and outputs.

modelAnswer: A system is an organized set of components coordinated to perform a designated function.
Every system has an objective or goal that it aims to fulfil.
Its components are its building blocks; each plays a specific role and contributes to the system's functioning.
The environment includes everything external to the system that interacts with it and can affect its operation.
Communication and interaction among components help them work together in an organized way to achieve the system's objectives.
Systems also interact with their environment through inputs and outputs.
For example, a weather monitoring system receives data from environmental sensors and provides weather status and forecasts to users.

For environment terms, distinguish static from dynamic and deterministic from non-deterministic using the definitions in your textbook.
Marks are earned for naming each feature and explaining its role, not just listing terms.

explain.title: What is a system?
explain.body: An Information System is simply an organized set of components that are coordinated to perform a designated function. A system's parts are related, and the way they work together helps the whole system operate.

explain.title: Objectives and components
explain.body: A system's objective is its purpose or goal. Components are the building blocks of a system; each has a role and contributes to the system's overall functioning. For example, the human brain processes information from the senses.

explain.title: Environment and interaction
explain.body: The environment of a system includes everything external to the system that interacts with it. Systems interact with their environment through inputs and outputs. The environment may be static or dynamic, and the impact of an output may be deterministic or non-deterministic.

explain.title: Communication
explain.body: Communication and interaction among system components help them work together in an organized way to achieve the system's objectives. For example, the CPU communicates with memory to fetch and store data.

mistakes: Do not define a system as only a group of parts; explain that the components are coordinated to perform a function or achieve an objective.
Do not confuse a system's objective with its components: the objective is the goal, while components are the parts that contribute to it.
Do not mix up the environment and the system itself. The environment is external to the system and interacts with it.
Do not confuse static with deterministic: static describes whether the environment changes independently, while deterministic describes whether the output's impact is known and certain.
When explaining communication, say how components interact to help achieve the system's objective.
